messages:
leah: Heads-up: ap-southeast1 nvme pool `temp-scratch-b1` is hammering IOPS between 00:10-00:40 UTC. GPU attach queue started to back up and we saw ~30 attach_timeouts. :(
dario: Ugh. Any quick metrics or sample logs?
leah: Pulled a short `iostat -x 1 3` from one host:
```
Device: rrqm/s wrqm/s r/s w/s rkB/s wkB/s avgrq-sz avgqu-sz await svctm %util
nvme0n1: 0.00 0.00 12.00 760.00 192.00 6200.00 8.20 9.50 9.9 1.20 97.7
nvme1n1: 0.00 0.00 8.00 650.00 128.00 5400.00 8.10 10.80 11.4 1.05 99.2
```
leah: kube-scheduler logs show repeated `attach_timeout` from pods trying to allocate GPUs at 00:15:21.
kim: Looks like janitor/cleaner activity plus a batch job release window. Two quick mitigations: lower janitor concurrency for that pool, and add a soft IO class (ionice/cgroup) for scrub jobs so they don't preempt attach I/O.
fin: If we reserve capacity what's the monthly delta? Need a ballpark for finance.
kim: Back-of-envelope: reserving 8 GPUs in ap-southeast1 is ~ $5k/mo, 16 GPUs ~ $9.5k/mo. (will refine if needed)
dario: Can we do an immediate canary: reduce janitor concurrency from 32->8 on 12 hosts and tag batch attaches to fallback pool? If that works we automate divert logic.
leah: I can push a canary now. Patch snippet:
```yaml
janitor:
  pools:
    temp-scratch-b1:
      concurrency: 8  # was 32
      scrub_priority: low
```
redwoodctl apply --cluster ap-southeast1 --patch janitor/temp-scratch-b1.yaml --scope canary:12
```
ops-bot: Applied patch on 12 hosts in ap-southeast1 for pool "temp-scratch-b1". Monitoring hooks: nvme.util, gpu.attach.latency.p95/p99.
leah: After ~8m into canary, attach_timeouts dropped from 30->2 and `gpu.attach.latency.p95` went from 1.9s -> 220ms. p99 still at ~1.1s for a few hosts.
dario: Good short-term. Next: (1) add auto-divert rule when nvme.util > 90% for 3m, (2) create a dedicated scratch-batch pool for noisy releases, (3) evaluate reserving 8 GPUs for high-SLO services. I'll open tickets.
kim: I'll draft the PR for auto-divert + ionice wrapper for janitor. Also propose moving janitor heavy work to off-peak window (02:00-05:00 local) for the region.
fin: Finance ok with a small pilot (8 GPUs) if we have clear SLO improvement metrics. Please include estimated monthly cost + SLO delta in the ticket.
leah: Filed ENGINFRA-4902 with links to graphs and the canary output. Assigning to @kim and @dario.
ops-bot: Runbook note created: "If nvme.util > 85% and gpu.attach latency p95 > 500ms, reduce janitor concurrency and trigger fallback pool allocation".
leah: Leaving dashboards pinned and will monitor next 6 hours: https://dashboards.redwood/internal/d/attach-health/ap-southeast1. Thanks all, canary looks good but will follow up with PR/metrics. :white_check_mark:
